title: The emerging role of microbiota in neuro-oncology
title_zh: 神经肿瘤学中微生物的新兴角色
abstract: Primary and metastatic brain tumours are associated with poor clinical outcomes, largely owing to limited therapeutic advances and an incomplete understanding of brain tumour biology. Increasing evidence suggests that microbial communities play an important part in shaping systemic immunity and tumour biology. Microbes and microbial by-products from the gut and oral cavity can influence the central nervous system through the gut-oral-brain axis, providing potential mechanisms by which distant microbes shape the brain tumour microenvironment. A growing body of literature has identified distinct gut and oral microbial signatures associated with brain tumours and demonstrated that microbiota modulation can influence tumour growth and treatment response in preclinical models. In addition, emerging clinical data indicate that primary and metastatic brain tumours can harbour intracellular microbial elements. In this Review, we summarize current knowledge on the roles of the gut and oral microbiota and intratumoural microbial elements in brain tumour biology and treatment response. We present the technical challenges inherent to microbial studies in brain tumours due to low biomass and the high risk of contamination, and discuss key clinical, experimental and computational considerations needed for rigorous experimental design and standardized methodologies. Last, we discuss translational opportunities and future directions for moving the field towards clinical impact.
abstract_zh: 原发性和转移性脑肿瘤临床预后不良，主要原因是治疗手段有限和脑肿瘤生物学认知不完整。越来越多的证据表明，微生物群在塑造系统免疫和肿瘤生物学方面起着重要作用。肠道和口腔微生物及其代谢产物可通过肠-口-脑轴影响中枢神经系统，为远处微生物如何塑造脑肿瘤微环境提供了潜在机制。大量文献已确识别出与脑肿瘤相关的特定肠道和口腔微生物特征，并证明微生物调节可在预模型中影响肿瘤生长和治疗反应。此外，新兴的临床数据表明，原发性和转移性脑肿瘤可能携带细胞内微生物成分。在本综述中，我们总结了肠道和口腔微生物以及肿瘤内微生物成分在脑肿瘤生物学和治疗反应中的现有知识。我们阐述了脑肿瘤微生物研究固有的技术挑战，因低生物量和高污染风险而存在，并讨论了严谨实验设计和标准化方法所需的关键临床、实验和计算考量。最后，我们讨论了转化机会和未来方向，以推动该领域向临床影响发展。
